To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the majority of Medicare beneficiaries with ischemic stroke die or are rehospitalized within one year of hospital discharge, 2) there are wide differences among hospitals in these rates of death or re-hospitalization, 3) these differences persist after risk adjustment, and 4) there are no improvements in death and re-hospitalization rates from 2003 through 2006.

30-day and one-year mortality and rehospitalizations for acute ischemic stroke vary considerably among hospitals in the United States, and that there has been little improvement over a four-year period.
1-year mortality and death or rehospitalisation after acute ischemic stroke were high, but varied widely by hospital.
